occurrences.source_assessment: Table 1 defines five different equal-ratio formulations using SRCHD03/04 (Brevundimonas diminuta), SRCHD05/07 (Brucella pseudintermedia) and SRCHD06 (Ochrobactrum sp.). A sixth formulation adds Micrococcus luteus SRCHD02. The species statements derive from partial 16S characterization, not demonstrated membership of the experimental genomes in GTDB clusters. C1-C5 suspended-culture endpoints and C6 immobilization/irradiation results are separate experiments. Keep two separate stock descriptors, their COMMUNITY_LEVEL participants, C1-specific 24/48/72-hour outcomes and single-isolate growth kinetics without a new intermember arrow. Preserve every original NCBI identity, source-local stock code, consortium ratio, participant descriptor, quotation, discussion and historical event. Only selected GTDB blocks/statuses/options and new native events may change. AS broth contains organic nutrients; bulk substrate/COD changes and ammonia production do not establish complete mineralization, consortium ammonia removal, interspecies flux or reciprocal benefit. Preserve 37 degrees Celsius suspended C1-C5, 24/48/72-hour Table 2 endpoints, monoculture kinetics and C5/C6 growth profiles as distinct evidence. Do not transfer C6 biofilm, gamma irradiation or immobilized per-carrier values to C1-C5. Preserve existing empty causal edge lists and the single COMMUNITY_LEVEL node per record. GTDB reference populations and option counts are unrelated to equal-ratio inoculation, viable-cell numbers or removal percentages. Do not infer a verified crosswalk release from file mtime. Keep differing GTDB and NCBI names explicit without renaming study stocks.
occurrences.population_scope: Preserve NCBI Brucella pseudintermedia and both distinct source stock names. The GTDB Ochrobactrum correspondence is an explicitly differing reference classification, not a formal renaming or exact study-stock assembly identification.
occurrences.name_scope: Preserve NCBI Brucella pseudintermedia and both distinct source stock names. The GTDB Ochrobactrum correspondence is an explicitly differing reference classification, not a formal renaming or exact study-stock assembly identification.
